doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Why she chose music over sprinting
summary: Running and music both gave her freedom; she argues for music and art in schools.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well you know I’m very glad the day that you had the conflict with the piano exam and the race, that you chose the piano exam. Because if you think about it, for one thing your career as a sprinter would probably be over by now.

You have to be so good. I mean even to just get, you know what I mean? I enjoy it. In fact I still want to run fast sometimes. I mean like I’ll be doing a jog and I’m like let me see if I’ve still got it. You know, but that also was about freedom and expressing myself with that freedom. You know when I was running I felt free of the world. It wasn’t a single thing that I was searching for, it was that I was trying to get it through two different ways. Music gave me the out of being disconnected from reality and church and school and bullies and all the stuff you go through as kids, and that’s why they’ve got to make more importance of music and art in schools, because kids needs to escape in a productive way. It’s true. And running was also, I know sports gets a lot of attention, but kids need to be active. They need to have healthy lives. And I think when you’re a kid — you’ll have some time to get fat, because you know what I mean? Because you want to be fit.
